sentences.text: Misc. Criminal Case No. 49549 of 2024

Rajendra @ Raghuraj @ Omprakash
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh

Appearance:
 Shri Manoj Saxena - Advocate for the applicant.

Shri Mukesh Parwal - Public Prosecutor for the responde
 Order

This is fourth bail application under Section 439 of Cr.P.C for grant of regular bail in connection with crime No.881/2022 dated : not mentioned, registered at P.S. - Rajgarh District - Rajgarh for offences punishable under Sections 419, 420, 467, 468, 471, 120-b, 201, 204 of IPC.
The first bail application was rejected on merit.

2. Counsel for the applicant submits that after first bail application, the applicant filed another application i.e. M.Cr.C No.19528/2024 which was dismissed as withdrawn with liberty to revive the application in case if the trial is not concluded within the period of 4 months.
The said order was passed on 12/7/2024 but the trial has yet not been concluded.
The applicant is in jail since 20/12/2022.
3. Considering the same, a status report was called from the trial Court.
As per the status report out of 26 witnesses, so far only 5 witnesses have been examined and 21 are yet to be examined.
Even the complainant has yet not been examined.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:722 2 MCRC-49549-2024 4.
Counsel for the State opposes the prayer for grant of bail.

sentences.text:
After hearing learned counsel for the parties and without adverting to the merits of the case, on the ground of incarceration period and the status report this Court is of the view that the trial may take time, therefore, the applicant is entitled for grant of bail on following conditions:
A) That the applicant shall not threaten the complainant or influence his witnesses during the pendency of trial.
B) The applicant shall mark his presence before the concerned Police Station once in every two months during the pendency of trial.

6. It is directed that applicant Rajendra @ Raghuraj @ Omprakash shall be released from custody upon furnishing a personal bond of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty thousand Only) with one surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the Ld. Court below.
7. A typed copy of this order is being forwarded to the Office of the Advocate General, on their email address, for intimation to the Police Station concerned.
The office is directed to forward a copy of this order to the Ld. Court below.
8. With the aforesaid, the application is allowed and disposed off.
Cc as per rules.

(VIJAY KUMAR SHUKLA) JUDGE PK Rajendra @ Raghuraj @ Omprakash vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/154502203/
